title: Interior design: where to start if you don't know your style yet
seo_title: Interior Design in Kyiv: Where to Start Without a Style
description: Interior design in Kyiv: where to start when you haven't chosen a style yet. Life scenarios, budget, references, layout and project cost from $30 per m².
lead: Many people put off interior design because they “haven't settled on a style yet”. Here is where to start with interior design in Kyiv when there is no clear picture in your head — and why style is far from the first question.

body: h2
Why style is not the first question
p

Words like “modern”, “Scandinavian” or “loft” sound like an answer to the question “what do you want?”, but in reality they are only a shell. Two interiors in the same style can be completely different to live in: in one, the kitchen is positioned so you can see the living room and the children from it; in the other, it is tucked into a dead end. Style is easy to change at the materials and decor stage, whereas a poor layout is almost impossible to fix once the renovation is done.
p

So if you don't know your style, that is no reason not to start. A designer will help you find it from your habits and preferences, but that needs a starting point — not a picture, but your life in this space.
h2
Where to actually start
p
It is worth answering a few practical questions. They would take an hour of conversation, but everything that follows depends on them.
ul
Who lives in the apartment or house and how that might change: children, parents, pets, guests.
What an ordinary day looks like: do you work from home, do you cook every day, where do you relax in the evening.
What needs storing: clothes, sports equipment, appliances, seasonal items, collections.
Which furniture and appliances you want to keep, and what you will buy new.
What budget you are prepared to put into the renovation and furniture together, not just one line item.
p

The answers to these questions are called life scenarios. They determine how many bedrooms you need and where they go, whether you need a separate walk-in wardrobe, the size of the dining table and how much storage there should be. This is what the brief for the designer is built from.

h2
How to collect references without the chaos
p

References are not a collection of two hundred pictures from social media. A pile like that only confuses: it has minimalism, classic and a bright accent all at once, and which of them is really yours is anyone's guess. It is better to keep it short and to the point.
ol
Choose three to five images that give you the feeling “I want to live right here”.
For each one, write a single sentence on what exactly you like: the light, the wall colour, the wood texture, the ceiling height, the tidy table.
Separately, save one or two pictures of what you definitely don't like — that is just as useful.
Show the designer the selection without explanations and see what they find in common.
p
Usually three to five images are enough to see the direction: warm or cool, light or deep, plain or decorated. That is the beginning of your style — without any labels.
h2
Layout before decor
p

Once the life scenarios are known, the designer proposes several layout options: where the kitchen goes, where the wardrobe is, how you move between rooms, which way the doors open. This is the most important stage of the project, and it should be approved before colours, tiles and light fittings. If the layout is comfortable, even simple decor looks expensive. If it isn't, the best materials won't save it.

h2
What an interior design project includes and what it costs
p

An interior design project is more than pictures. It includes a survey, the layout, 3D visualisations, working drawings, specifications and an estimate. For the detailed list of documents and why each one matters, see our article on [what an interior design project includes](/en/blog/what-is-included-in-interior-design-project).
p

At CAS Development, interior design costs from $30 per m², with a minimum project budget of $2,500. For reference: for a 100 m² apartment that is from $3,000. The exact figure comes from the estimate after the survey and brief.
p

It is also worth thinking separately about who will carry out the project. The same team that designed it can deliver it: turnkey renovation from $550 per m² and furnishing from $250 per m². h2
The first step: survey and brief
p
To start, you don't need to know your style or have references ready. You need two things.
ul
A survey of the premises: exact dimensions, heights, the position of windows, risers and the electrical panel.
A brief: a conversation about your family, habits, budget and the furniture you want to keep.
p

After that the designer proposes the first layout options, and the style begins to emerge on its own: from your answers, your references and the solutions you like more. You are not guessing — you are choosing from options.
